# The Weaver of Stars

Long ago, before humans counted time, there lived a weaver named Astra in a village at the edge of the world. While others wove cloth from wool and cotton, Astra dreamed of creating something eternal.

One night, she climbed the highest mountain and reached toward the moon. The celestial goddess, moved by such boldness, granted her a single strand of moonlight. Astra wove through the night, her fingers dancing across an invisible loom, pulling threads from the darkness itself.

As dawn approached, she had created a magnificent tapestry—but it was unlike any earthly fabric. When she held it up, it dissolved into the sky, and where each thread had been, a star now gleamed.

The goddess returned and spoke: "You have woven beauty that belongs to all. For this selflessness, you shall continue your work forever."

Astra became the constellation we call the Weaver, visible each autumn night. When new stars appear in the heavens, astronomers say they are simply discovering what was always there. But the poets know better—they are witnessing Astra's eternal work, weaving light into the darkness, creating beauty for all humanity to share.

# The Tale of the First Shadow

In the beginning, the world was filled only with light. The Sun Goddess, Solara, ruled over everything, and her brilliance touched every corner of existence. All creatures lived in endless day, never knowing rest.

One day, a young weaver named Nyx grew exhausted from the eternal brightness. She worked her loom without ceasing, for there was no darkness to signal when to stop. Her eyes burned, and her body ached for respite.

In desperation, Nyx wove a cloth from the darkest threads she could find—midnight blue, deep violet, and charcoal black. She worked for what seemed like ages, creating a tapestry so dense that no light could penetrate it. When finished, she held it above her head.

For the first time, darkness fell upon the earth. Beneath her creation, Nyx felt cool relief. Her eyes closed, and she discovered sleep.

Solara saw this and understood. She made a pact with Nyx: each day, the weaver would unfurl her cloth across half the world, giving all creatures rest. In gratitude, Solara named this gift "night" and appointed Nyx its eternal guardian.

Thus, shadow was born from compassion, and balance came to the world.

Myth: In the time before seasons, three guardians dwelt apart in the new world—Ember, keeper of growth and warmth; Frost, holder of rest and preservation; and between them, Whisper, who carried only gentle breezes and understood neither extreme.

Ember blazed across the land, making plants grow so rapidly they exhausted the soil and withered. Frost swept behind, freezing everything so deeply that seeds could never wake. The world became a wasteland of burned earth and barren ice.

Whisper wandered the devastated middle ground, grieving. In desperation, she called both guardians to meet her. "Your powers are destroying what they should nurture," she said. "Let me show you another way."

She asked Ember to warm the frozen ground gently while Frost held back. Seeds stirred and sprouted. Then she invited Frost to cool the burning growth while Ember rested. Plants matured and set new seeds before sleeping.

"Alone, you harm," Whisper explained. "But flowing through me, taking turns, you create life's rhythm."

The guardians agreed to work in cycles, with Whisper mediating their transitions. Thus spring, summer, autumn, and winter were born—each season a dance of giving way, a lesson that neither dominance nor absence serves the world, but rather the graceful exchange of gifts in their proper time.
